title: Demand-Driven Context: A Methodology for Coherent Knowledge Bases Through Agent Failure
talk_summary: A staff engineer at IKEA describes 'demand-driven context': instead of pushing a monolithic knowledge base into agents via RAG/MCP, you give agents real work items, let them fail, have them emit an explicit checklist of missing/undocumented knowledge, fill those gaps, and have the agent curate the new knowledge into a structured, versioned store (GitHub). He automates this as a 'context gap scanner' that runs historical incidents against the knowledge base to produce a prioritized Kanban of documentation gaps.

takeaways.what_they_do: Give the agent a real work item; on failure it must output a confidence score plus an explicit checklist of missing terminology/business logic, which a human fills; the agent then curates the answer into the knowledge base.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it gives a checklist of things. So, we fulfill the checklist
takeaways.numbers: confidence rose from ~1.4 to 4.4 over 14 incident cycles

takeaways.technique: Context gap scanner over historical work items
takeaways.what_they_do: Batch-run past incidents/tickets against the knowledge base to score each as clean/stale/incomplete/missing, then consolidate into a prioritized Kanban of documentation gaps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: validate each incident across my knowledge base and ask the agent ... how much of the documentation is I can't trust it

takeaways.technique: Knowledge base as a git repo with PR review
takeaways.what_they_do: Store curated context blocks in a GitHub repo so multi-agent/multi-team contributions get PR review, conflict resolution, and permissions for free; publish elsewhere from there.
Structure the knowledge base to mirror business-process→system→API relationships so agents can navigate rather than guess which of many files to open.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your file structure is actually a representation of your meta model. It actually knows how to navigate

takeaways.technique: Whole-domain context over RAG when it fits
takeaways.what_they_do: Measured ~96K tokens per domain consolidated; argues just putting the whole domain context in the window beats graph-RAG until you approach ~1M tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just putting the whole context right now in the window gives you more results than actually doing uh uh rag

takeaways.what_they_do: Scanner output becomes a prioritized board (critical/high/medium) of documentation tasks that get worked like Jira tickets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will create a Kanban board for you ... just like Jira tickets, we finish it
